title: Shelter the homeless
hookLine: the holy family had no room
tomorrow: what did Job's friends get right, before they said a word?

lines: AN AIR MATTRESS ON THE FLOOR.
NO ROOM FOR THEM IN THE INN.
cards: An air mattress on a friend's floor. A cousin's couch for a week that turns into a month. Maybe you've slept somewhere that wasn't yours.
Now Luke's Christmas story. A couple far from home, Mary with child, and her time comes.
And the reason the baby ends up in an animal's feed box is one plain line, in the Douay-Rheims: "because there was no room for them in the inn." So where's the innkeeper? Nowhere.

teach.b: No door slammed in anyone's face, no cruel landlord. Those come from Christmas plays, not from the Gospel. Luke says only that there was no room.
Then the king in Matthew 25, the next line in his list: "I was a stranger, and you took me in." He doesn't ask how the stranger came to have nowhere to go. He remembers who opened a door.
The prophet Isaiah, describing the fast God wants, says: "bring the needy and the harbourless into thy house."
The Douay keeps that old word for people with no safe place to put in. And the Catechism names sheltering the homeless among the bodily works of mercy.
Today it might be a parish hall opened on freezing nights, a family hosting a refugee, a couch offered after a breakup, a gift that keeps a shelter's lights on. And it turns inward too.
Making room can start with whether there's space for one more at a table, in a week, in a life.

how: Catholic parishes and charities run shelters and winter overnight programs, host refugee families, and support housing work as one of the corporal works of mercy.

o: give a place to stay to someone with nowhere to go
keep your own home open only to close family
build new churches in towns that don't have one

s: Luke's Gospel has an innkeeper who turns Mary and Joseph away
Luke says only that there was no room in the inn. the innkeeper comes from Christmas plays.
the king in Matthew 25 asks how the stranger became homeless
he only remembers who took the stranger in.
Isaiah links bringing the homeless in to the fast God wants

games.q: your neighbor's kid, eighteen, got kicked out after a fight at home. his mom says he 'made his choices.' what does the king's line ask first?
o: find out whose fault the fight was before helping.
make sure he has somewhere safe tonight; the reasons can wait.
stay out of it, since it's another family's business.
games.why: the king doesn't ask how the stranger came to have nowhere to go. he remembers who opened a door.

practice: Close your eyes and see your own front door, and a few of the people who have walked through it. Then see someone with no door tonight, in a shelter, a car, on a friend's floor, and stay with them quietly.
If you pray, pray for them in your own words.

wordCard.voice: Shelter the homeless. Open a door, or help keep one open, for someone with nowhere to stay.

orig.note: Greek, the word Luke uses for the inn, a lodging place.

carryVoice: Your line: make room. Luke's sentence was about room, and so is this whole work of mercy. That's the week.
